findings.title: set_thermal_parameters DHW minimums written mid-solve are silently reverted by the away-setback unwind
findings.claim: A set_thermal_parameters call carrying dhw_min_temperature and/or dhw_idle_min_temperature that lands while async_run_optimization is awaiting its solve is acknowledged, applied, and then overwritten with the pre-solve values by the unconditional away.restore_setback in async_run_optimization's finally, even with away mode inactive; the reverted values are what every later solve uses and what the coordinator publishes.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py:4754 snapshots six fields via away.apply_setback, which returns the originals even when no setback is applied (away.py:301-302); the solve then awaits the process worker for seconds (the whole async_run_optimization body incl. shadow solves); coordinator.py:5027 restore_setback writes the six snapshotted values back unconditionally, clobbering any loop-side write made in between. set_thermal_parameters (services.py:handle_set_thermal_params -> coordinator.async_update_thermal_params) is an in-memory writer of two of those fields (dhw_min_temp, dhw_idle_min_temp) that runs on the loop during that await.

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_run_optimization (finally -> heatpump_optimizer.away:restore_setback); heatpump_optimizer.services:handle_set_thermal_params; coordinator:_run_in_process hooked to detect in-flight

perturbation.change: away.py:302 `return original` -> `return None` (no setback applied => the finally's `if away_original is not None` skips the unwind); harness flag --perturb applies it in-process and restores it

findings.metric_definition: Of dhw_min_temp and dhw_idle_min_temp set by a set_thermal_parameters call made mid-solve, count those != requested after the cycle returns (live ctx params and coordinator.data).
findings.phenomenon_property: No loop-side write accepted while a solve is in flight may be undone by the solve's own snapshot-and-unwind; an unwind restores only fields it actually changed, and only if nobody wrote them since.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n 'apply_setback\|restore_setback\|away_original' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/away.py ; writers of the six snapshotted fields: grep -nE '\.(target_temp|min_temp|comfort_temp_day|comfort_temp_night|dhw_min_temp|dhw_idle_min_temp) *=|"dhw_min_temperature": "dhw_min_temp"' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py

reproduction_steps: run the command; race arm prints live=(45.0,20.0) published=(45.0,20.0), control arm (38.0,31.0)

window: setback_window_max_s_provisional=5.8 s on this loaded box (apply_setback -> restore_setback), i.e. ~0.3 % of the default 30-min interval here; larger on a Pi; also covers the first background solve after every setup/reload
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.async_run_optimization / away.apply_setback+restore_setback: unwind only when a setback (or economy/open-window widening) was applied, and restore a field only if it still holds the value the envelope wrote (compare-and-restore); alternatively apply the setback to the _solve_snapshot copies instead of the live ctx objects. Add a real-loop test that writes mid-solve.

findings.title: diagnose_interval service runs a bound coordinator method on the executor, touching live state off the loop
findings.claim: services.py:handle_diagnose_interval passes coord.diagnose_last_interval to hass.async_add_executor_job, so an executor thread reads _ctx (live _thermal_params) and _last_interval_record and writes _last_diagnosis on the live coordinator, bypassing the _diagnose_payload deepcopy snapshot the Diagnose button path (async_diagnose_interval) uses; it is the only off-loop coordinator access in the lifecycle.
findings.mechanism: services.py:965-967; the button path coordinator.async_diagnose_interval -> _await_process(diagnosis.diagnose_record, *_diagnose_payload(self)) deep-copies params and runs in the worker process. The service path shallow-copies the live params (dataclasses.replace) on a thread while the loop may be inside async_run_optimization with the setback/aperture/economy mutations applied, and runs the model in-process holding the GIL.

findings.metric_definition: Distinct single-underscore coordinator attributes read or written from a non-loop thread across setup, two solves, a what-if, the diagnose service and the Diagnose button.
findings.phenomenon_property: No executor job receives the live coordinator (or a bound method of it); everything a thread needs crosses as a snapshot, as _solve_snapshot/_diagnose_payload do.
findings.seam_rule: grep -nE 'async_add_executor_job\((coord|self)\.|_await_process\([^)]*(coord|self)\.' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py ; and PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 tools/audit/round8/D1/s1_thread_reads.py

findings.proposed_fix_scope: services.handle_diagnose_interval: call coord.async_diagnose_interval() (or _await_process with _diagnose_payload) and read the report back; no production behaviour change beyond the snapshot.

non_findings.claim: Real-loop lifecycle (ThreadPoolExecutor executor, scheduled tasks, entry state machine with per-entry setup_lock, LIFO on_unload, background-task cancel): setup -> first background solve -> reload mid-solve -> unload mid-solve -> setup again leaves no live task, loop timer, bus/state listener referencing a torn-down coordinator, both torn-down coordinators are collected, no exception escapes, no store save or service call after unload, the stale solve never lands on the old instance (#237 latch), and both new instances complete their first real solve. The harness moves: --perturb-no-cancel (skip the in-flight cancel and drop the latch) gives old_solve_landed_after_unload 0->2, released_latch_set 1->0.

non_findings.claim: The old solve's executor thread is still inside coordinator._run_in_process when reload/unload returns (cancelling the asyncio task does not stop the concurrent future); it keeps _PROCESS_LOCK until the child answers and the new instance's first solve queues behind it and completes. Latency only, not a wedge.
